adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's country overview sets out the national framework a trans visitor to the Riau Islands stands under, with no Riau Islands-specific divergence on the page: private same-sex conduct is not criminalised nationally but attracts no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections, legal gender change requires sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and the amended penal code criminalising extramarital sex - passed December 2022, in force from 2 January 2026 - carries up to one year in prison when a complaint is lodged. The page also documents Indonesia voting against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity in 2016, 2022 and 2025, a 2025 Pew figure of 93% of Indonesians rating homosexuality morally unacceptable, and a 2023 Pew estimate of 95% opposition to same-sex marriage; a 2020 raid case shows enforcement of such moral rules varies locally ('released because no regional regulation exists'). This grounds the record's at-national-score assessment in dated, sourceable national specifics since no province-specific source was surfaced.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's country overview supplies the national framework East Kalimantan is assessed under, with no East Kalimantan-specific entry on the page: private same-sex conduct is not criminalised nationally but enjoys no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections, legal gender change is conditional on sex-reassignment surgery plus judicial approval, and the amended penal code outlawing extramarital sex - passed December 2022, effective 2 January 2026 - is punishable by up to one year in prison on complaint. It records Indonesia voting against the UN independent expert on sexual orientation and gender identity in 2016, 2022 and 2025, a 2025 Pew finding that 93% of Indonesians view homosexuality as morally unacceptable, and a 2023 Pew estimate of 95% opposition to same-sex marriage. The page's local-regulation material (for example a 2021 Bogor city bylaw and a 2020 raid in which a gay transgender couple was released for lack of a regional regulation) corroborates that subnational regulation varies by district, consistent with the record's claim about provincial-level divergence, though the eight-province list itself is not enumerated here and continues to rest on the existing Diplomat source.
